title: Gabriele Münter's birth chart
metaDescription: Gabriele Münter's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 1.0° Pisces. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Moon stands at 9.9° Taurus, in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun sits at 1.0° Pisces — the first decan, 0°–10°, which the tradition sub-rules by Jupiter. Degrees matter more than the sign label here: two people born a fortnight apart share Pisces and share almost nothing else about where the Sun actually stood.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: Mercury holds 4.3° Aquarius, Venus holds 11.6° Aquarius, Mars holds 23.4° Sagittarius — in the old shorthand, a mind at home in argument and pattern; taste led by wit and proportion; drive that ignites on contact.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The day's firmest angle joins Uranus and Pluto — a square holding at 0.3°. Nothing in a square flows; everything in it works. The old texts kept squares for the charts they respected. Behind it, Mars trine Uranus at 1.1°, and Mercury square Neptune at 1.4° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: The day-stable angles form no closed figure. Nothing funnels; each aspect is its own negotiation, which the tradition reads as a chart of separate treaties rather than one campaign.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The classical table has two entries for this chart. The Moon in Taurus at 9.9° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Jupiter in Sagittarius at 28.5° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. Condition, not character: that is all the dignity table ever measured.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Among the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the elements divide 3 earth, 3 fire, 2 water, 2 air; by modality, 6 fixed, 4 mutable. An earth emphasis reads as patience with material reality — slow hands, durable results. Uranus was retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Taurus for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 13.0° between midnight and midnight. The sign survives the missing hour; the degree does not, and is given as a reference rather than a fact. At the noon reference it stands at 9.9°.
